author: ribeye
dek: DC's mud-monster horror topped the box office with $24 million — and one Falcons fan's Halloween date night went exactly as his wife predicted.
disclaimer: Parody: the Nowak family of Bowling Green is fictional. The Clayface box office opening is real, as reported by the Associated Press in October 2026.
headline: Bowling Green Dad Survives R-Rated Clayface, Loses a Bet, and Is Now Legally Required to Admit His Wife Was Right

ohio_story: BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — Tom Nowak of Bowling Green walked into the theater on Main Street on Saturday night a skeptic and walked out a convert — mostly because his wife, Dana, had bet him twenty bucks he would hide behind the popcorn before the first jump scare, and she collects her debts promptly. "I did not hide," Tom said, standing in the lobby with butter on his shirt. "I merely lowered my face toward the popcorn for tactical reasons. There is a difference. Dana says there is not a difference. Dana has my twenty dollars."

The couple had planned the night as a proper Halloween-weekend date: dinner downtown, a walk past the Bowling Green State University campus, and then the new DC horror movie Dana had been talking about since the trailer dropped. Tom, a lifelong Falcons fan who considers the scariest thing in his life to be the Doyt Perry Stadium concession line at halftime, lasted about forty minutes before asking — loudly, according to witnesses — whether the mud man "could maybe fight someone with a hose." Dana, who grew up on horror movies and considers a 9 p.m. showing on a Saturday night to be a sacred trust, did not pause the movie. She did, however, hold his hand during the surgery scene, a fact Tom denies and Dana has already told her sister.

By the credits, Tom was already ranking the movie above every superhero film he'd seen this year and texting his son, a BGSU sophomore, to ask if he'd caught it yet. "The mud guy had a rough week, and honestly, so did I," Tom said. "But Dana was right. Dana is usually right. I have budgeted accordingly for next weekend, when she picks the movie again."
real_summary: DC Studios scored a modest, R-rated win with "Clayface," which landed a $24 million opening weekend, according to studio estimates reported Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. In 3,458 theaters, the Warner Bros. release narrowly edged A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything," which pulled in $19.5 million in its first weekend of wide release.

"Clayface" stars Tom Rhys Harries as Matt Hagen, a rising movie star who undergoes experimental facial surgery after a mob boss disfigures him. It is the third theatrical release for DC under the stewardship of James Gunn and Peter Safran, and a bid to meld body horror with a comic book movie. While such an opening would have been a flop for most superhero films, "Clayface" was budgeted at only $44 million — a fraction of the expense of most comic book films — and added $19 million internationally. Audiences gave it an "A-" CinemaScore, a high grade for a horror release.

The opening offered some stability to DC Studios following the disappointment of "Supergirl," which grossed just $126 million worldwide on a $170 million production budget earlier this year. Elsewhere at the box office, Laika's stop-motion animated "Wildwood" debuted in third place with $11.8 million, while last weekend's top film, the video game adaptation "Street Fighter," sank 72% to $8.6 million in its second weekend.
source_note: AP reporting, Oct 2026: Clayface opens at No. 1 with an estimated $24 million domestic weekend, Oct. 23-25, edging You Can See Everything at $19.5 million.
